newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Outgoing PM says Estonia stable, transition over.
newsitem.headline: Outgoing PM says Estonia stable, transition over.

text.p: Outgoing Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said on Wednesday the small Baltic state had stabilised and was over the period of transition from a former Soviet republic to a market economy.
Vaehi is stepping down after nearly losing a no-confidence earlier this month. He says he wants a stronger coalition to be formed than the current minority administration.
"Estonia has stabilised, has become a state and is regarded as a partner in international relations," Vaehi told parliament as he formally told MPs of his decision to quit.
"The transition period is over," he added.
Vaehi yesterday handed his resignation to President Lennart Meri, two weeks after announcing he would quit.
Vaehi came to power after elections in March 1995 and some reformists feared he would try and slow down the pace of reforms set by a previous radical free market government.
But reform has continued and Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states with a population of just 1.5 million, is seen as one of the success cases of the former Soviet Union.
But the transition period was tough, with inflation soaring to more than 1,000 percent at one point and output slumping.
"The economy is past its lows and there is growth in share prices and lower inflation," Vaehi added.
"The government is not taking liquidity from the banks and banks are not going bankrupt," he added.
Vaehi's Coalition Party has already chosen its preferred candidate as next prime minister in the shape of Mart Siiman.
Siiman is head of the parliamentary party of the Coalition Party. In order formally to begin talks on forming a new government he has to be asked to be prime minister by Meri.
